deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page is a heavily corrected draft of §§3–4 of Riemann's 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines gleichartigen flüssigen Ellipsoides' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 9, 1861). In that paper the motion of the homogeneous ellipsoid is split into (i) the rotation of the principal axes ξ, η, ζ in space and (ii) an internal motion relative to those axes. The quantities u, v, w, u', v', w' and the direction-cosine table α, β, γ, …, γ'' appear there. The system called (A) is a linear system of first-order ODEs. It is satisfied by the direction cosines of the body axes with respect to any line fixed in space. In modern terms these are Poisson's kinematic equations dγ/dt = γ × Ω, written in the body frame, for a vector fixed in space.

Paragraph 1 (struck draft) and paragraph 2 (rewritten version):
(a) Every real solution of (A), multiplied by a suitable constant, gives the cosines of the angles that the axes ξ, η, ζ make at time t with some fixed line. [Mine: (A) is linear and preserves |γ|², because γ·(γ×Ω)=0. So a real solution of constant norm, normalised, is a unit vector fixed in space.]
(b) Earlier Riemann found three independent solutions.
- The first is the conserved angular-momentum-type vector. Its fixed line is the normal to the invariable plane of the whole moving mass.
- The other two are complex conjugates. Their real and imaginary parts correspond to two mutually perpendicular lines lying in the invariable plane.
(c) The cosines of the axes with respect to that normal are 𝔩/ω, 𝔪/ω, 𝔫/ω. Here (𝔩, 𝔪, 𝔫) are the body-frame components of the conserved vector and ω = sqrt(𝔩²+𝔪²+𝔫²) is constant. They follow from the solution of the equations (α) by elimination, without any further integration.
(d) The complete orientation then needs only one quadrature. This gives the angle ψ through which the plane spanned by the normal and the ξ-axis has turned since t = 0.
- Draft paragraph 1 gives an explicit integrand, read as ∫ (g k + k' k'')/(k² + k'²) dt. The letters are uncertain.
- [Mine] The standard formula has the form dψ/dt = ω (Ω_η 𝔪 + Ω_ζ 𝔫)/(𝔪² + 𝔫²). Here Ω is the angular velocity of the axes and the denominator is the sum of the squared components of the conserved vector perpendicular to ξ. This is the structure of Riemann's fraction: a bilinear numerator over a sum of two squares.

Paragraphs 3–4 (several struck attempts): for an ellipsoid with two equal axes, the initial position of the axes is not fixed by the shape of the fluid mass. It depends in general also on the initial motion. It stays arbitrary only if the motion keeps the axes equal at all times. Riemann remarks that his form of the equations is well suited to integration and to actually determining the motion. It is less suited to a general proof that the motion is possible (existence and continuation of solutions). One reason is that its derivation is less simple. Another is that equality of two axes needs separate treatment, so the general argument splits into many special cases. This links to the previous page.

Last paragraph: before looking for special integrable cases of (A), note the sign symmetries of the system. Any change of signs of the 𝔩, u, v, w, … is admissible as long as the products such as uω, u'ω' (the read products are uncertain) are unchanged. Two cases follow.
(1) Interchanging the primed and unprimed quantities simultaneously transposes the cosine table α, β, …, γ'' and the table 𝔩, 𝔪, …: 'Horizontalreihe mit Verticalreihe vertauscht'. Each motion thus has an adjoint motion in which the roles of the axis rotation and the internal vorticity are swapped. This is Dedekind's reciprocity theorem (1860). The first words of the next page complete the sentence: '...der von [Dedekind] gefundene Reciprocitätssatz'.
(2) Reversing the signs of two of the pairs (u,u'), (v,v'), (w,w') amounts to reversing one coordinate. It carries the motion into its mirror-image motion.
errors: No mathematical errors are detectable. The page is a draft with many cancellations, and several symbols are illegible.

The integrand of the precession quadrature, read as (gk+k'k'')/(k²+k'²), cannot be verified from the image. The letters may be misread. Its structure (bilinear numerator over a sum of two squares) is what the correct formula requires.
The claim that the motion is undetermined only when two axes are equal is stated without proof. It is correct as a qualitative remark.

results.what: Solutions of the linear system (A) are, up to a constant, the direction cosines of the body axes with respect to fixed lines in space. One fixed line is the normal to the invariable plane; the real and imaginary parts of the complex solutions give two perpendicular lines in that plane.
results.modern_name: Poisson kinematic equations / conserved angular momentum fixing the invariable plane (Euler–Poinsot-type reduction)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, Poisson, Poinsot (rigid body); for the fluid ellipsoid, Dirichlet/Dedekind/Riemann 1857–61

results.what: Orientation relative to the invariable-plane normal follows algebraically. The remaining angle (rotation of the ξ-axis about the normal) follows from a single quadrature.
results.modern_name: Precession angle by quadrature (reconstruction of the rotation from body-frame angular momentum)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (rigid body, 1849); Riemann 1861 for the Riemann ellipsoids

results.what: Transposing the cosine matrix (swapping primed and unprimed quantities) maps solutions to solutions.
Sign reversal of two of the pairs (u,u'), (v,v'), (w,w') gives the mirror-image motion.
results.modern_name: Reflection symmetry of the Riemann/Dirichlet ellipsoid equations

results.what: With two equal axes, the orientation of the axes is not determined by the shape, so a general existence argument must treat many special cases.
results.modern_name: Degeneracy of the principal-axis frame for spheroids

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of passages that appear essentially unchanged in Riemann's published 1861 paper on the fluid ellipsoid. That paper includes the geometric meaning of the solutions of (A), the single quadrature, the equal-axes remark and the reference to Dedekind's reciprocity. Nothing goes beyond the published text.

checkable.asserts: Equals 0 in a test configuration with the ξ-axis at fixed polar angle th from the normal. The precession rate about the normal is (Ω_η 𝔪 + Ω_ζ 𝔫)/(𝔪²+𝔫²) times ω (here ω=1). This is the structure of Riemann's single quadrature.

Equals the zero matrix. Transposing the factors of the linear deformation map gives the adjoint motion; this is the algebraic core of Dedekind's reciprocity (swap of the horizontal and vertical rows of the cosine tables).

transcription_corrections: Paragraph 2, 'der ganzen festen [?] Masse': read 'der ganzen bewegten Masse', as in paragraph 1 and the published text.

The sentence at the bottom of the page continues onto the next page as 'Hiernach besteht der von [Dedekind] gefundene Reciprocitätssatz'. The next-page fragment 'Bedeutung [?] gefundenen' should be read as 'Dedekind gefundenen'.
'die Größen α, β, …, γ'' mit den Größen α, β, …, γ'' [?]': the sense is that the tables α…γ'' and 𝔩…𝔫'' are interchanged or transposed (rows ↔ columns), not identical lists.
'u, v; v, w; u', w' [?]': the pairs are most likely (u,u'), (v,v'), (w,w'), as in the next page.

The fraction in paragraph 1, read 'gk+k'k''/(k²+k'²)', is uncertain. It probably involves the angular velocity components times the components of the conserved vector, over the sum of two of its squared components.
